thread.title: Consumer Tech To Hit Record $351 Billion In 2018: CES

author: Barron's
title: Consumer Tech To Hit Record $351 Billion In 2018: CES
text:
Bloomberg News LAS VEGAS -- Consumer technology will extend its reach and influence in the U.S. economy in 2018, rising 3.9% to a record $351 billion in retail revenue, according to the Consumer Technology Association.
The semi-annual industry report, released shortly before the start of the Consumer Electronics Show (CES) here, includes for the first time a projection for consumer spending on music and video-streaming services, which it says will account for $19.5 billion.
The CTA, which oversees and operates CES, says it included audio and video services from the likes of Apple (ticker: AAPL), Hulu (HULU), Netflix ( NFLX ) and others to "capture" the evolving consumer tech experience.
CTA officials expect continued growth for emerging technology such as wearables ($6.4 billion), smart speakers ($3.8 billion) and virtual reality ($1.2 billion) -- as well as another strong year for stalwarts like smartphones ($62.9 billion), laptops ($28.4 billion), digital TVs ($22.1 billion) and automotive electronics ($15.9 billion).
"Technology is improving our lives in more ways than ever -- and consumer enthusiasm is growing just as quickly as companies can bring their innovations to market," CTA CEO Gary Shapiro said in a statement on Sunday. He added the optimistic forecast is predicated on a strong stock market, continued job growth and "stable" rules for international trade.
